tool.name: ParaFEM Mesh Import
tool.description: Convert Abaqus .inp mesh to ParaFEM format using inp2pf
tool.command: cp '$inp_file' job.inp && #if str($renumber) == "yes" inp2pf -renumber job.inp 2>&1 && #else inp2pf job.inp 2>&1 && #end if mv job.d '$output_d' && mv job.nset '$output_nset' && echo "ParaFEM Mesh Import Summary" > '$output_summary' && echo "---------------------------" >> '$output_summary' && grep "*NSET" '$output_nset' | while read -r line; do count=\$(echo \$line | awk '{print \$2}') name=\$(echo \$line | awk '{print \$3}') echo "NSET: \$name (\$count nodes)" >> '$output_summary' done

param.name: inp_file
param.label: Abaqus .inp file
param.help: Mesh file in Abaqus .inp format. Export from GMSH, FreeCAD, Salome, etc.

tool.help:
Converts an Abaqus .inp mesh file to ParaFEM format using inp2pf.
Only the geometry (.d file) is retained. Physics-specific files (.dat, .bnd, .fix) are generated by the downstream BC generator tool.
Supported Abaqus element types: - C3D8, C3D8R, C3D8I (8-node hexahedron) - DC3D8 (8-node hex, diffusion/thermal) - C3D20, C3D20R (20-node hexahedron) - C3D4, C3D10, C3D10R (tetrahedra)
Workflow: Create geometry in a GUI tool (GMSH, FreeCAD, Salome) -> export as Abaqus .inp -> import here -> feed to BC generator.
The -renumber option ensures contiguous node/element IDs starting at 1, which is required by ParaFEM.
